lines: Clock generator with ten divisions from sixteenth notes to thirty-two bars, plus a run button, a reset button and a voltage copy of its rate setting
Sets the clock speed, from one pulse every 4 seconds counter-clockwise to 64 pulses a second clockwise, counted in sixteenth notes
Restarts the count from the first sixteenth and fires a 1ms pulse at the reset output
Starts and stops the clock, one press each way, and restarts the count from the first sixteenth
Carries a 1ms pulse each time the count is restarted by the reset button, and a 10ms pulse each time the run button is pressed
A 10ms pulse on every sixteenth note, at the speed set by RATE
A 10ms pulse on every eighth note, one for every two sixteenths
A 10ms pulse on every quarter note, one for every four sixteenths
A 10ms pulse on every half note, one for every eight sixteenths
A 10ms pulse once a bar, one for every sixteen sixteenths
A 10ms pulse every two bars, one for every thirty-two sixteenths
A 10ms pulse every four bars, one for every sixty-four sixteenths
A 10ms pulse every eight bars, one for every 128 sixteenths
A 10ms pulse every sixteen bars, one for every 256 sixteenths
A 10ms pulse every thirty-two bars, one for every 512 sixteenths
Carries the RATE setting as a voltage, -2V fully counter-clockwise to 6V fully clockwise
Note — Time Expansion placed immediately to the right of this module takes its clock from it, and produces nothing without it
TimeDiktat.notes: The clock stops counting while the run button is off, so the reset button does nothing until it is on again.

lines: Expander for Time Diktat, placed immediately to the right of it: six clock divisions gated by chance, and six outputs carrying one division with another's pulses removed
Sets the chance that a pulse of that division reaches its output, none counter-clockwise to every pulse clockwise; it is drawn afresh on each pulse
Attenuates the voltage at the probability input for that division, adding it to the chance set by that division's own probability knob
Shifts the chance for that division, scaled by that division's MOD. knob; 10V with MOD. fully clockwise makes every pulse pass
Carries the sixteenth-note pulses of Time Diktat that pass the chance set for them
Carries the eighth-note pulses of Time Diktat that pass the chance set for them
Carries the quarter-note pulses of Time Diktat that pass the chance set for them
Carries the half-note pulses of Time Diktat that pass the chance set for them
Carries the one-bar pulses of Time Diktat that pass the chance set for them
Carries the two-bar pulses of Time Diktat that pass the chance set for them
A 1V pulse on every eighth note that is not also a quarter note
A 1V pulse on every sixteenth note that is not also a quarter note
A 1V pulse on every sixteenth note that is not also a half note
A 1V pulse on every eighth note that is not also a half note
A 1V pulse on every quarter note that is not also a half note
A 1V pulse on every half note that is not also the first beat of a bar
Note — every probability knob starts at zero, so nothing reaches the six gated outputs until one is raised, and the module is silent as it is placed
TimeExpansion.notes: The probability and modulation knobs carry no range or name in the code, so Rack gives them the default 0 to 1 with a default of 0: every gated output is silent until its probability knob is raised. A thirteenth output exists in the code but is not placed on the panel.

lines: Two eight-step sequencers, each with a row of pitch sliders, two rows of trigger buttons, and thinned copies of both trigger rows
Advances that sequencer by one step on each rising edge; its trigger outputs stay high for as long as this stays high
A trigger here returns that sequencer to its first step
Sets how many steps that sequencer plays before returning to the first, 1 to 8
Sets the voltage that step sends to the CV output of its sequencer, 0-10V
Turns that step on or off for the TRG 1 output of its sequencer
Turns that step on or off for the TRG 2 output of its sequencer
Sets the chance that a step's trigger reaches the TRIG 1A output, none counter-clockwise to every one clockwise, though the chance used is a tenth higher than the setting the panel's PROB. shows
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the probability input, adding it to the chance set by PROB.
Shifts the chance set by PROB., scaled by the MOD. attenuverter
Carries a 10V gate while the clock is high on a step turned on in the first trigger row
Carries the gate of the first trigger row only on the steps that pass the chance set by PROB.
Carries a 10V gate while the clock is high on a step turned on in the second trigger row
Carries the gate of the second trigger row on about one step in four, drawn afresh each time and not adjustable
Carries the voltage of the current step's slider, 0-10V
Picks the factor the step voltage is multiplied by for the scaled output: 0.1, 0.2 or 0.5
Inverts the scaled output of that sequencer
Carries the current step's voltage multiplied by the scaler setting, inverted where INV is engaged
SequenceModeler.notes: The chance on the TRIG 1A outputs is the PROB. setting plus 0.1, because the code adds a tenth while the step's gate is high. The TRG 2A outputs are fixed at 0.25 by the same arithmetic and read no knob. Two further thinned outputs and a run button exist in the code but are not placed on the panel.

lines: Quantizer with twelve semitone buttons, its own random source for when nothing is patched in, and a sample and hold clocked from the trigger input
Picks the factor the pitch is multiplied by before quantizing: 0.1, 0.2 or 0.5. It always scales the internal random source, and scales a voltage at CV IN only while ON is engaged
Applies the scaling factor to a voltage patched into CV IN
Allows the root, 0V, into the set of notes the output is quantized to
Allows the note one semitone above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note two semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note three semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note four semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note five semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note six semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note seven semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note eight semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note nine semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note ten semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
Allows the note eleven semitones above the root into the set the output is quantized to
The pitch to be quantized, a volt per octave; with nothing patched here the module quantizes its own random voltage instead
A trigger here samples the quantized pitch and holds it at the output until the next trigger
A trigger here glides the output to the held pitch over the following 100ms, in place of stepping to it
A voltage here is added to the pitch before it is quantized
A voltage here is added to the pitch after it is quantized, so it shifts the output off the chosen notes
The quantized pitch, held until the next trigger
Note — with no semitone button lit the output holds the last note it reached
Eight-input sequential switch for pitch voltages, with a scaler on the chosen input and a transposed variation of it triggered by hand or by gate
Sets how many of the eight inputs are cycled through, 1 to 8
Selects that input, making it the one the output carries
One of the eight voltages the switch chooses between
A trigger here returns the switch to the first input
A trigger here moves the switch on to the next input
A trigger here replaces the output with the transposed variation for the time set by LENGTH
A voltage here shifts the LENGTH time, scaled by the MOD. attenuverter
Sets how long the transposed variation lasts, from 10ms counter-clockwise to 1 second clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the MOD input, adding it to the LENGTH time
Picks the factor the chosen input is multiplied by while ON is engaged: 0.1, 0.2 or 0.5
Inverts the scaled voltage while ON is engaged
Applies the scaler, and the INV switch, to the chosen input
Sets the octaves the variation is transposed by, -2 to +2
Sets the semitones the variation is transposed up by, 0 to 11
Carries the chosen input, scaled where ON is engaged, and the transposed version of it while a variation lasts
PitchIntegrator.notes: Input 10 in the code sets the number of steps from a voltage, but no jack for it is placed on the panel. The octave and semitone transposition reaches the output only during a variation.

lines: Eight-input sequential switch for triggers, with a burst clock of its own that replaces the output for a moment on command
Sets how many of the eight inputs are cycled through, 1 to 8
Selects that input, making it the one the output carries
One of the eight signals the switch chooses between
A trigger here returns the switch to the first input
A trigger here moves the switch on to the next input
A trigger here replaces the output with the burst clock for the time set by LENGTH
A voltage here shifts the LENGTH time, scaled by the MOD. attenuverter
Sets how long the burst lasts, from 10ms counter-clockwise to 1 second clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the MOD input, adding it to the LENGTH time
Picks the burst rate as a multiple of the RATE setting: two pulses for the thirty-second, about three for the forty-eighth, four for the sixty-fourth
Sets the speed the burst rate is multiplied up from, 0.25 to 64 pulses a second
A voltage here replaces the RATE knob, each volt doubling the speed
A trigger here restarts the burst clock from the start of a pulse
Carries the chosen input, and the burst clock for the length of a burst
BurstIntegrator.notes: Input 10 in the code sets the number of steps from a voltage, but no jack for it is placed on the panel.

lines: Four LFOs drawn from one clock, each with its own division and skew, feeding two averaging mixes, with sampled copies of every wave
Sets the speed the four LFOs are divided down from, 0.25 to 64 cycles a second
A voltage here replaces the RATE knob, each volt doubling the speed
A trigger here samples all four waves and both mixes, holding them at the STEP outputs until the next trigger
A trigger here restarts that LFO from the start of its cycle
Sets how far that LFO is divided below the RATE speed, in ten steps from sixteenth notes to thirty-two bars
Bends that LFO into an exponential curve, which holds it near 0V for longer and sharpens its peak
Moves the peak of that LFO within its cycle, a rising ramp counter-clockwise, a rounded hump at noon and a falling ramp clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the skew CV for that LFO, adding it to that LFO's SKEW setting
A voltage here shifts that LFO's skew, scaled by that LFO's S. MOD attenuverter
That LFO, 0-10V, rising to 10V and back to 0V once a cycle
That LFO's voltage as it was at the last STEP CLOCK trigger, held until the next one
Switches that LFO into that mix, which averages every LFO switched into it
The average of the LFOs switched into that mix, 0-10V
That mix as it was at the last STEP CLOCK trigger, held until the next one
A trigger here samples both mixes, holding them at the pair of alternate step outputs
That mix as it was at the last trigger on the alternate clock, held until the next one
Note — an LFO is computed only while one of its outputs is patched or it is switched into a mix; otherwise its outputs hold their last value
QuadModulator.notes: The jack marked STEP CLOCK is called a global reset in the code, but no reset is carried out: a trigger there only clocks the sample and hold, after a 5ms delay. Eight parameters in the code have no widget on the panel.

lines: Eight-step trigger sequencer with two rows, each row also giving a copy of its triggers thinned by chance
Advances the sequencer by one step on each rising edge; the trigger outputs stay high for as long as this stays high
A trigger here returns the sequencer to its first step
Sets how many steps play before the sequencer returns to the first, 1 to 8
Sets the chance that a step's trigger reaches the two thinned outputs, none counter-clockwise to every one clockwise, though the chance used is a tenth higher than the setting the panel's PROB. shows
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the probability input, adding it to the chance for the TRIG1A output alone
Shifts the chance for the TRIG1A output, scaled by the MOD. attenuverter
Turns that step on or off for the TRIG1 output
Turns that step on or off for the TRIG2 output
Carries a 10V gate while the clock is high on a step turned on in the first row
Carries the first row's gate only on the steps that pass the chance set by PROB.
Carries a 10V gate while the clock is high on a step turned on in the second row
Carries the second row's gate only on the steps that pass the chance set by PROB.
ImpulseControl.notes: The chance actually used is the PROB. setting plus 0.1, because the code adds a tenth while the step's gate is high. A third output and a second probability input exist in the code but are not placed on the panel.

lines: Two phase-distorted sine oscillators, one modulating the phase of the other, with a mix between them and a clipper on the main output
Sets the carrier pitch in whole octaves, -2 to +2
Raises the carrier pitch in semitones, 0 to 12
Trims the carrier pitch, ten cents down counter-clockwise to ten cents up clockwise
Sets the modulator pitch in whole octaves, -2 to +2
Raises the modulator pitch in semitones, 0 to 12
Trims the modulator pitch, ten cents down counter-clockwise to ten cents up clockwise
Sets the carrier pitch, a volt per octave, added to the carrier's octave, coarse and fine settings; 0V gives C4 at 261.63Hz. The modulator follows it while the modulator pitch jack is empty
Sets the modulator pitch, a volt per octave, in place of the main pitch voltage
Moves the breakpoint of the carrier's phase-distortion curve earlier in the cycle, from halfway through to a tenth of the way through, brightening the tone
Runs the carrier's sine through more of its cycle before the breakpoint, up to two full turns clockwise, adding harmonics
Moves the breakpoint of the modulator's phase-distortion curve earlier in the cycle, from halfway through to a tenth of the way through, brightening it
Runs the modulator's sine through more of its cycle before the breakpoint, up to two full turns clockwise, adding harmonics
Attenuates and inverts one phase-distortion CV, adding it to the XMOD or YMOD setting that CV modulates
A voltage here shifts one phase-distortion setting, scaled by its own attenuverter; 10V with that attenuverter fully clockwise covers the whole range
Sets how far the modulator's output bends the phase of the carrier, silent counter-clockwise to an index of 3.3 clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FM jack, adding it to the FM setting
A voltage here shifts the FM amount, scaled by the FM attenuverter
Crossfades the main output between the carrier counter-clockwise and the modulator clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the mix jack, adding it to the MIX setting
A voltage here shifts the mix, scaled by the mix attenuverter
Crossfades the main output into a copy of itself gained five times and squared off at the limits, clean counter-clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the clip jack, adding it to the CLIP setting
A voltage here shifts the clipping, scaled by the clip attenuverter
The carrier and modulator blended as set by MIX and clipped as set by CLIP, ±5V
The carrier alone, with the modulator bending its phase, ±5V
The modulator alone, ±5V
Four channels of transposition for pitch voltages, one adding whole octaves and one adding semitones
Adds a whole number of volts to that channel's octave input, -5 to +5, an octave a step
The pitch voltage the octave offset is added to
The pitch voltage at that channel's octave input with the octave offset added
Adds semitones to that channel's semitone output, 0 to 11, a twelfth of a volt each
Transposes that channel's semitones downwards rather than upwards
The pitch voltage the semitone offset is added to
The semitone offset on its own, or added to the voltage at that channel's semitone input where one is patched
Transposes the second channel's semitones downwards rather than upwards, though with nothing patched into that channel's semitone input it inverts the first channel's amount instead
QuadSteppedOffset.notes: In the second semitone channel the inverting switch reads the first channel's knob while nothing is patched into its own input, so it transposes by the first channel's amount. The other three channels are correct.

lines: Four scalers, four two-input adders and four voltage-controlled amplifiers, in one panel
Picks the factor the voltage at that scaler's input is multiplied by: 0.1, 0.2 or 0.5
The voltage to be scaled down
The scaler input multiplied by the factor its switch is set to; 0V while nothing is patched in
One of the two voltages that row adds together
The two voltages patched into that row, added together
The signal that amplifier passes, scaled by the voltage at its CV input
Sets the gain of that amplifier, silent at 0V and unity at 10V, with voltages above that amplifying further
The signal input of that amplifier multiplied by its CV input divided by ten
Adds a slow random drift to a pitch voltage, on two independent channels
The voltage to be drifted; nothing patched here leaves that channel's output at 0V
Sets how often a new random value is drawn for that channel, once a second counter-clockwise to eight times a second clockwise, and shortens the glide between values as it rises
Scales the drift added to that channel's input, none counter-clockwise to a few hundredths of a volt clockwise
The input voltage of that channel with its drift added
Driftgen.notes: The second channel glides to each new value faster than the first at the same rate setting; the slew constants differ in the code.

lines: Percussion voice: one phase-shaped sine or white noise through a resonant filter, with a decay envelope, a pitch-bend envelope and an accent envelope
Sets the pitch of the voice in whole octaves, 4 to 12, where 8 gives C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the pitch of the voice, a volt per octave, added to the octave setting
Sets how far the bend envelope raises the pitch, silent counter-clockwise to five octaves clockwise
Sets how much of each cycle is held at 0V before the sine runs, a tenth to nine tenths of it, brightening the tone as it rises
Attenuates and inverts the width CV, adding it to the WIDTH setting
A voltage here shifts the WIDTH setting, scaled by the X MOD. attenuverter
Crossfades the voice between the sine counter-clockwise and white noise clockwise
Sets the pitch of the modulating sine against the voice, two octaves down counter-clockwise to three octaves up clockwise
Sets how far the modulating sine bends the pitch of the voice
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FM jack, adding it to the FM depth
A voltage here shifts the FM depth, scaled by the FM attenuverter
A trigger here starts the main envelope and the bend envelope, and restarts both oscillators from zero phase
A voltage sampled here at each trigger scales the level of the audio output, silent at 0V and full at 10V
A trigger here starts the accent envelope
Sets the decay of the main envelope, 1ms at the bottom to about 1 second at the top
Sets the decay of the bend envelope, 1ms at the bottom to about 1 second at the top
Sets the decay of the accent envelope, 1ms at the bottom to about 1 second at the top
Multiplies the decay range of the main envelope by ten, reaching about 10 seconds
Multiplies the decay range of the bend envelope by ten, reaching about 10 seconds
Multiplies the decay range of the accent envelope by ten, reaching about 10 seconds
Attenuates and inverts the main envelope's decay CV, adding it to that envelope's decay time
Attenuates and inverts the bend envelope's decay CV, adding it to that envelope's decay time
Attenuates and inverts the accent envelope's decay CV, adding it to that envelope's decay time
A voltage here shifts the decay of the main envelope, scaled by that envelope's MOD. attenuverter
A voltage here shifts the decay of the bend envelope, scaled by that envelope's MOD. attenuverter
A voltage here shifts the decay of the accent envelope, scaled by that envelope's MOD. attenuverter
The main envelope, 0-10V, jumping to 10V at a trigger and falling at the time set for it
The bend envelope, 0-10V, jumping to 10V at a trigger and falling at the time set for it
The accent envelope, 0-10V, jumping to 10V at an accent trigger and falling at the time set for it
Sets the filter cutoff, about 33Hz fully counter-clockwise to about 16kHz fully clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the main envelope where it is added to the filter cutoff
Sets the resonance of the filter, flat counter-clockwise to a sharp peak at the cutoff clockwise
Attenuates and inverts one of the two cutoff CVs, adding it to the filter cutoff; each volt moves the cutoff an octave at the full setting
A voltage here shifts the filter cutoff, scaled by its own attenuverter
Switches the filter between lowpass and highpass
The bare oscillator, sine to noise as set by SOURCE, about ±5V, with no envelope and no filter
The voice after the main envelope, the velocity level and the filter, ±5V
PercussiveVibration.notes: Three parameters and four inputs in the code, among them a first-harmonic level and a separate reset, have no widget on the panel. The accent decay slider carries no range in the code, so Rack gives it the default 0 to 1, which matches the other two sliders.

lines: Synth voice: up to three phase-shaped sine oscillators, frequency-modulated by a chosen set of their own harmonics, with one envelope
Sets the pitch of the voice in whole octaves, 4 to 12, where 8 gives C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the pitch of the first oscillator, a volt per octave, added to the octave setting
A pitch voltage here adds a second oscillator at that pitch, mixed equally with the first into both audio outputs
A pitch voltage here adds a third oscillator at that pitch, mixed equally with the first into both audio outputs
Sets where the breakpoint of the phase-shaping curve falls in the cycle, a tenth to nine tenths of the way through
Attenuates and inverts the width CV, adding it to the WIDTH setting
A voltage here shifts the WIDTH setting, scaled by the XMOD attenuverter
Sets how far the wave has advanced at that breakpoint, 0 to 0.9; at 0.5 with WIDTH at 0.5 the wave is an unshaped sine
Attenuates and inverts the curve CV, adding it to the CURVE setting
A voltage here shifts the CURVE setting, scaled by the YMOD attenuverter
Sets the level of the lowest of the three harmonics chosen by SET in the modulating signal
Sets the level of the middle of the three harmonics chosen by SET in the modulating signal
Sets the level of the highest of the three harmonics chosen by SET in the modulating signal
Attenuates and inverts the level CV for that harmonic, adding it to that harmonic's slider setting
A voltage here shifts one harmonic's level, scaled by that harmonic's MOD AMT attenuverter
Picks which three of the second to sixth harmonics make up the modulating signal, in eight combinations
Sets how far the harmonic mix bends the pitch of the oscillators, silent counter-clockwise to seven clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the envelope where it is added to the FM level
Attenuates and inverts one of the two FM level CVs, adding it to the FM level
A voltage here shifts the FM level, scaled by its own attenuverter
Sets the rise time of the envelope, from the shortest time of the chosen range counter-clockwise to the longest clockwise
Sets the fall time of the envelope, from the shortest time of the chosen range counter-clockwise to the longest clockwise
Picks the envelope's time range: 1ms to 1 second on fast, 10ms to 10 seconds on medium, 100ms to 100 seconds on slow
Bends the rise and the fall of the envelope into an exponential curve
Makes the envelope start again as soon as it reaches 0V, so it runs as an LFO with no trigger
Chooses what the envelope's modulation voltage changes: the rise alone, the fall alone, or both
Attenuates and inverts the envelope's modulation voltage, adding it to the time chosen by DEST.
A voltage here shifts the envelope time chosen by DEST., scaled by the MOD attenuverter
A trigger here starts the envelope
The envelope, 0-10V
The oscillators mixed together, ±5V, with no envelope applied
The oscillators mixed together and scaled by the envelope, ±5V
AdditiveVibration.notes: An envelope trigger button exists in the code but is not placed on the panel.

lines: Two envelopes from one trigger: one opens an amplifier on a crossfade of two signals, the other reaches a jack as control voltage
A trigger here starts both envelopes
Sets the rise time of the envelope that opens the amplifier, 10ms counter-clockwise to about 10 seconds clockwise
Sets the fall time of the envelope that opens the amplifier, 10ms counter-clockwise to about 10 seconds clockwise
Sets the rise time of the envelope sent to the CV output, 10ms counter-clockwise to about 10 seconds clockwise
Sets the fall time of the envelope sent to the CV output, 10ms counter-clockwise to about 10 seconds clockwise
One of the two signals the MIX knob crossfades between; this one is carried with MIX fully counter-clockwise
One of the two signals the MIX knob crossfades between; this one is carried with MIX fully clockwise
Inverts the modulation voltage where it changes the fall time of the envelope sent to the CV output
Makes the envelope sent to the CV output start again as soon as it reaches 0V, so it runs as an LFO with no trigger
Crossfades the amplifier's input between the first signal input counter-clockwise and the second clockwise
Attenuates the voltage at the mix jack, adding it to the MIX setting
A voltage here shifts the crossfade, scaled by the mix attenuverter
Attenuates and inverts the modulation voltage, adding it to the envelope time chosen by DEST.
A voltage here shifts the envelope time chosen by DEST., scaled by the MOD. attenuverter
Chooses what the modulation voltage changes in both envelopes: the rise alone, the fall alone, or both
The crossfade of the two signal inputs, scaled by the envelope that opens the amplifier
The envelope that CYCLE loops, 0-10V, shaped by its own rise and fall settings
TornArtery.notes: Only the modulation destination and amount carry a range in the code; the rise, fall, mix, invert and cycle controls fall back to Rack's default 0 to 1 with a default of 0. The two signal inputs carry whatever is patched into them, so they are given no family.
